chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from someone else, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is befitting for the performer of Tamattu' with the Umra to the Hajj, when he is free from Ihram, that he should not wear a shirt, and let him resemble the ones in Ihram.

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: He became free from Ihram (after Umra rituals)
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umra and Hajj)
key_terms.قَمِيصاً: A stitched shirt (one of the prohibited items for men in Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended dress code for a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' after entering Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the spiritual continuity of the Ihram state for those performing Hajj al-Tamattu', instructing them to refrain from wearing a stitched shirt (qamis) to maintain uniformity with other pilgrims. This practice underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on outward humility and the symbolic shedding of worldly distinctions during the sacred rites, reinforcing the unity of the pilgrim community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from someone else, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is befitting for the performer of Tumatto with the Umra to the Hajj, when he is free from Ihraam, that he should not wear a shirt, and let him resemble himself with the ones in Ihraam’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy from more than one person who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is very proper for one who is for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous), that after coming out of the state of Ihram, he should not dress up with a shirt to remain like those in the state of Ihram.’”
